headline: Japan visit: PM Tarique Rahman secures $6.3B investment and 200k jobs
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's summit with Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi focuses on energy security, high-tech cooperation, and strategic partnership.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has hailed his visit to Japan as an "important step forward" for the strategic partnership between the two nations, announcing potential gains including billions in investment and the creation of approximately 200,000 jobs.

During a summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, the two leaders discussed emergency financial assistance of 50 billion yen (about $320 million) under the Partnership for Power Asia initiative to strengthen Bangladesh's energy security.

The leaders explored the possibility of up to 1 trillion yen (around $6.3 billion) in Japanese private-sector investment over the next five years, which is expected to accelerate industrialization and expand manufacturing capacity.

PM Tarique Rahman proposed the establishment of a Bangladesh-Japan Tech Park to promote cooperation in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, robotics, electronics manufacturing, and other advanced technologies.
The discussions also covered space science, satellite engineering, and Japanese support for a high-speed rail network linking six major divisional cities, alongside modern transport infrastructure.

A key outcome was the commitment to advance the Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B) initiative under a new framework for shared prosperity, integrating energy, deep-sea ports, and regional connectivity.
The leaders also discussed the early implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement and the creation of a ministerial-level joint commission to ensure concrete results.
PM Tarique Rahman thanked Japan for its continued humanitarian assistance to the Rohingya people and called for their voluntary, safe, and dignified return to Myanmar.
caption:
Up to $6.3 billion in investment and 200,000 new jobs. PM Tarique Rahman's visit to Japan marks a major strategic leap.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has hailed his visit to Japan as an "important step forward" for the strategic partnership between the two nations, announcing potential gains including billions in investment and the creation of approximately 200,000 jobs.

During a summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, the two leaders discussed emergency financial assistance of 50 billion yen (about $320 million) under the Partnership for Power Asia initiative to strengthen Bangladesh's energy security.

The leaders explored the possibility of up to 1 trillion yen (around $6.3 billion) in Japanese private-sector investment over the next five years, which is expected to accelerate industrialization and expand manufacturing capacity.

PM Tarique Rahman proposed the establishment of a Bangladesh-Japan Tech Park to promote cooperation in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, robotics, electronics manufacturing, and other advanced technologies.

The discussions also covered space science, satellite engineering, and Japanese support for a high-speed rail network linking six major divisional cities, alongside modern transport infrastructure.

A key outcome was the commitment to advance the Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B) initiative under a new framework for shared prosperity, integrating energy, deep-sea ports, and regional connectivity.

The leaders also discussed the early implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement and the creation of a ministerial-level joint commission to ensure concrete results.

PM Tarique Rahman thanked Japan for its continued humanitarian assistance to the Rohingya people and called for their voluntary, safe, and dignified return to Myanmar.

headline: 13-0 defeat: Bangladesh concede 13 goals to India in opening match
summary: The men's hockey team suffered a massive loss at the Hero Asian Champions Trophy in Punjab, marking the third straight game with 10+ goals conceded to India.
details: Bangladesh began their Hero Asian Champions Trophy campaign on a disappointing note, suffering a 13-0 defeat to hosts India on Tuesday.
The match took place at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Punjab, India.
India dominated from the start, scoring in the second minute and leading 4-0 by the end of the first quarter.
By halftime, India had extended their lead to 6-0, continuing a relentless attack throughout the match.
In the third quarter, the five-time champions added three more goals, and the final quarter saw four more goals to complete the rout.
Mandeep Singh stood out for the Indian side, scoring a hattrick during the match.
This marks the third consecutive match in which Bangladesh has conceded more than 10 goals against India.
Previous losses included a 10-0 defeat at the Asian Games in Japan last September and a 12-0 loss at the 2023 Asian Games in China.
caption:
A crushing 13-0 loss. Bangladesh's hockey campaign starts with a massive defeat against India.

Bangladesh began their Hero Asian Champions Trophy campaign on a disappointing note, suffering a 13-0 defeat to hosts India on Tuesday.

The match took place at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Punjab, India.

India dominated from the start, scoring in the second minute and leading 4-0 by the end of the first quarter.

By halftime, India had extended their lead to 6-0, continuing a relentless attack throughout the match.

In the third quarter, the five-time champions added three more goals, and the final quarter saw four more goals to complete the rout.

Mandeep Singh stood out for the Indian side, scoring a hattrick during the match.

This marks the third consecutive match in which Bangladesh has conceded more than 10 goals against India.

Previous losses included a 10-0 defeat at the Asian Games in Japan last September and a 12-0 loss at the 2023 Asian Games in China.
